agree.reason: A judge would find the budget clear, but the closing paragraph turns a 'third attorney' request into a backfill, then a maybe-third, and that muddle weakens the case.

honest.reason: It says the new attorney will start before June, though the decision comes in May and the last hire took five months; it also adds the year 2027 to the October renewal and says the position doesn't depend on county money, which the facts don't establish.

works_the_facts.reason: The funding arithmetic ($78k − $45k − $20k = $13k) is correct and useful, but it never works out the 14% representation rate or that turn-aways (300) were nearly double the tenants served (163).

right_comparison.reason: 'One attorney after June' is a true no-grant baseline, but the 58% has no stated comparison and the draft doesn't say that none exists or that court-wide data will be requested.

qualification.reason: The county renewal gets a date but is waved away, not treated as a real risk, and the checkable commitments (six-month outcome reports, clerk data from January) are left out.

objections.reason: It answers 'how do you cover the rest of the cost' well, but not hiring lag, the missing comparison for the 58%, or what happens after two years, all of which the facts could have addressed.

fit.reason: At roughly 270 words it is under the 300-word limit and reads as a proper project summary, though the last paragraph is confusing.
